title: Dragon's Lair
build: Software Projects disk, alternate D64 with LA–LJ files

records.c: The first copied byte in the scene record is $01. The caller starts executing one byte later.
Save the caller stack pointer, then set escape $54 and scan the embedded source at $D010 for the end marker. Decode the aligned picture stream to $4000 before setting up the platform scene.
Read through the banked-out source until eleven bytes match END OF CODE at $1C40.
A zero byte between the jump back to scan the next source byte and the success branch target at $1E38.

Start the graphics stream at the page after the marker. Save the stream pointer at $2D42/$2D43 and decode up to $7FFF exclusive, then clear the padding byte at the end of each 64-byte block in $5000–$75FF.

Restore the saved stack and set the falling-platform colour row and glyph inputs. Request sound $84, install the raster handler at $28EB and rebuild the character matrices. Select the $4000 VIC bank and initialize the counters and sprite settings for the descent.
Feed alternating synthetic down and left input values to $2116 until sprite 0 X falls below $20.
Wait through two CIA2 timer periods, then call the descent updates in order. Repeat while $25 is zero and delay the return using $2D33 once it changes.
Test the byte at $2D33. Return on zero or continue into the jump update at $1FAA.

Call the platform update and check the jump-in-progress flag at $2AFC. A pressed fire bit starts a jump, clears its step index and checks the descent progression. An active jump advances the step index and selects the vertical displacement from the movement state and the table at $2D15.
Select the $4400 screen in $D018 and refresh its colours. Set up nine rows of fourteen patch characters from $2C04 and clear screen cell $4531 before applying the patch.
Select the $4800 screen for colour and VIC rendering. Use $2BAA as the source for a three-row, seven-cell overlay and set the screen and colour output pointers.
Synchronize with the raster, then return if $2AFC is nonzero. Otherwise clear $2D35 and continue at $2116 when the countdown at $28EA reaches zero.
Toggle between the sprite pose banks and select the base frame index. Test active-low up, down and horizontal input and use the corresponding four-piece frame tables.

Update the falling platform when $2AFA permits it. Depending on its flags and countdown, clear matching character cells in a 14-column strip over four rows, play the exit sequence and re-enter the scene initialization.

At zero countdown, scan four rows for character 2 or codes at least $3C and erase them, waiting between rows. Then enter the exit animation and restart. Other countdown values take the branch at $22D8.
Subtract $57 from sprite 2 Y and require a result below $17. Double that Y offset and subtract it and $DC from sprite 2 X to obtain the signed offset stored at $2D2A.
Store $FF in the scene byte at $2D27 and return.
Skip the update when $2B5E is zero. Otherwise disable the current fire movement, check the descent-distance threshold and update one of two obstacle states.
Read the obstacle countdown and branch to its next update if negative. Otherwise decrement it and toggle the sprite 4 enable bit.
Set the mirror flag from A and pass the sprite records in the $A2–$A6 and $AC–$B0 ranges through the shared transform routine. Enable sprites 0–4.
Load the delay and movement bytes at $2B61–$2B68 with their preset values and clear $2B6C.
Check the active countdown flag and the platform progress. When it reaches the scene threshold play the alternate screen sequence. Otherwise advance the nested countdowns and handle the timeout path.

Select a path from the screen matrix bits in $D018. With the first matrix selected, use the state and delay at $2D32 and $2D31 to decide between movement and fire input. Completing the other matrix path resets the movement fields and decrements the stage counters.
A standalone RTS between the jump at $277F and the alternate vertical offset entry at $2783.

Choose one of two vertical sprite updates from $2AFD. Both subtract the indexed offset at $2D15, adjust by at most one pixel using a scene flag, align the companion sprites and run three matrix refresh calls.
When the exit flag is set, update jump and platform state and retest the restart flag. With player high X set and low X at least $50, clear the timer gate and decrement the scene result byte.
Use the saved jump step to choose one of two four-frame groups. Select the table and mirror flag according to the direction in $2AFD, then install the four sprite pointers.
Clear nineteen screen cells on each of ten rows beginning at $4173. Then prepare the ten-row overlay read from $2CB4 and its corresponding colour writes.
The pose code at $2126 and $2D5B writes the active quartet index at $28E9. The main update decrements the timer at $28EA before advancing the pose.

Copy the eight sprite pointer slots and the associated screen bytes into the other two matrices. Advance the matrix timing countdown and change the VIC matrix selection after the next divider expires.
Add the step at $2D38 to the low X of sprite 0 and write it to all four player sprites. On carry set all four high-X bits.
Subtract the step at $2D38 from the low X of sprite 0 and give the result to all four player sprites. On borrow clear all four high-X bits.
Save the eight sprite pointers, restore the compressed picture source pointer from $2D42/$2D43 and decode character cells beginning at $4000, temporarily switching the processor port for each read.
Continue the matrix copy while the destination page is below $4C. On completion select screen page $40 through $03D6 and apply the resident VIC setup with $167A set to $77.
Select nine source rows at $2B7D, screen output $4069 and colour output $D869. Start the row width at fifteen cells.
Take the last column index from $03 and save the row width, index plus one, at $0E.
Copy source codes 0, 2 and $3C or greater to the screen and use the corresponding colour from $7700. Advance the source by fifteen cells and both destinations by forty after each row.

Use sprite 2 Y minus $22 and player X adjusted for the current high bit and horizontal position. Convert to character coordinates and calculate pointers for corresponding cells in each of the three matrices. The coordinate limit can set the timeout to $32 instead.
Set $2D37 to $32 if sprite 0 has high X clear and low X at least $EE, or if either corresponding alternate-matrix cell differs from the first matrix.
Initial divider value seven. The handler at $290F decrements it while the obstacle sequence is enabled, reloading seven on expiration.
Six bytes for descent state. The update at $227E tests $2AFA. The fire handler sets $2AFC during a jump. The movement code sets the direction at $2AFD and toggles pose bit 2 at $2AFE.
Values $40–$5F form a sequential pointer run immediately before the next four descent frame pointers at $2B1F. In the scene VIC bank those values address the 64-byte slots at $5000–$57FF.
Four VIC sprite pointers loaded in the movement paths at $224A and $225D.
Four companion VIC sprite pointers loaded by $2237 and $2270.
Two quartets of sprite pointers selected by toggling bit 2 of the pose index for ordinary movement.
Two quartets of sprite pointers selected in the direction cases that read at $2846 and $2859.
Two quartets for the other launch directions, read at $2833 and $286C.
Two quartets copied to the primary sprite pointer table by the waiting animation at $2D63.
Four consecutive VIC pointers chosen for the first strip of the exit animation at $2DB7.
Three consecutive pairs of VIC pointers read by the exit sequence at $2DCA, $2DD8 and $2DE6.
The two pointers $92 and $93 selected for expanded sprites during the exit.
Two groups of four pointers copied into slots 4–7 in the failure matrix $4C00.
Pointer $9C used following the two four-sprite failure animation poses.

The first-descent obstacle sequence counters and flags. At $2334, $2B5E enables the update, $2B5F divides the step and $2B5D counts repetitions. The sprite update at $2423 uses $2B61–$2B65 for enable and frame changes.
Four groups of four VIC coordinate bytes copied to the registers for sprites 4 and 5 by the obstacle updater.
Nine rows of fifteen character codes for $4069 and its subsequent rows. The loop at $2A39 examines each row from column 14 down to 0.
Nine rows of fourteen source character codes for the alternate matrix at $4400. The setup at $2088 selects this record and the copier looks up the colour of each cell through $7700.
Twenty-one additional cell codes between the 126 cells copied to the middle matrix and the far overlay. The same codes follow the middle overlay at $2CAE in the second descent.
Three rows of seven character codes beginning at $2C97, selected by the setup at $2601 for a patch in the matrix at $4800.
Four cell codes after the three seven-cell rows drawn in the far matrix and before the four transition cells read by $25C2–$25E1.
Four character codes written by $25C2–$25E1 to $47AD, $47B6, $47DD and $47DE in reverse source order.
Ten rows of character codes selected by $28B8. A row ends on $FF or at eighteen cells, before the output pointers advance by 40.
Eighteen cell codes following the ten consumed overlay rows, before the jump displacement table. They also follow the ten-row overlay in the second descent.
Seventeen signed offsets from the base vertical position for the first-descent jump frames. The jump arithmetic subtracts the indexed value.

The jump frame at $2D26 indexes the vertical offsets. The following bytes include direction and outcome flags, obstacle counters, the alternate matrix timer at $2D31, and the displacement used by the matrix refresh at $293E and $295E.
Eight sprite pointers saved by $297B and restored by $29E4 when the unpacker rewrites the matrix.
The scene initialization sets the reload to six. The timed matrix cycle at $26B2 copies it to $2D31.
Source pointer restored at $2984 to start graphics decoding from the embedded stream.
Clear the pending sound effect and cycle four sprite pointers over ten CIA2 waits. Select the fourth display matrix and its colour table for the follow-on animation.
Run 20 delayed updates. Subtract one from sprite 0 X and add one to its Y on each update, then call the sprite alignment routine at $2F30.

Select the $4C00 matrix and lookup page $76, enable sprites 4–7 and install their positions and colours. Request sound $8A and select the first four failure frame pointers from $2B53 for the timed animation.
Set all four low X coordinates equal. Use sprite 0 Y for sprite 1 and add $15 for the two lower sprites.
This scene record ends with the eleven byte marker copied by the unpacker at $0DDE.
The decoded VIC screen base. The first 256 character indices cover six full rows and the start of the seventh row.
Screen indices $100–$1FF reference the glyph data at $7800 during the falling platform scene.
Screen indices $200–$2FF form the lower section of the platform display. The graphics loader puts them here before play begins.
The last page of falling platform screen memory, with the sprite pointer table occupying the final eight bytes.
Alternate character matrix at $4400 selected by $D018=$1F. The scene updates cells such as $4531 and $47AD and fills its sprite pointer table at $47F8.
Third character matrix at $4800. The scene selects it with $D018=$2F and applies the colour lookup with source page $48.
Fourth character matrix at $4C00 selected by $D018=$3C in the sequence at $2D44. Sprite pointers for this matrix begin at $4FF8.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $5000–$53FF to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $5400–$57FF to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
The first ten sprite frames used as individual pieces for composite movement poses. The rendered pieces include sets of feet, tunic rows and upper body silhouettes.
Two 64-byte sprite images in slots selected by sprite pointers $6A and $6B. Sprites 2 and 3 selected these slots in the first-descent play capture.
Two 64-byte sprite records in slots $6C and $6D, selected by sprites 0 and 1 in the first-descent play capture.
Sixteen adjacent 64-byte records for the middle movement poses. Higher pointers show progressively shifted fragments of feet and body.
The final two 64-byte pieces in the middle movement sequence, addressed by sprite pointers $7E and $7F.
Sixteen 64-byte pieces for late platform poses. The bitmaps include outstretched limbs and angled footprints.
Two more 64-byte pose pieces at sprite pointers $90 and $91, immediately before the disc shapes.
Circular silhouettes and disc quadrants in slots $92–$9C. Shapes $94–$9B are quarter circles of two sizes.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $6740–$687F to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
Sprite records in slots $A2–$B0 showing round and irregular obstacle silhouettes.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $6C40–$7007 to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
Eighty eight-byte glyph records for character codes 1 through 80. The failure sequence sets $D018=$3C in VIC bank $4000, selecting $7000 as the glyph base and $4C00 as the screen matrix.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $7288–$75FF to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
Palette table for the fourth matrix. The scene sets the colour lookup high byte at $167A to $76 before processing the matrix at $4C00.
Palette table indexed by the active scene character matrix. The descent restores this table before recolouring the first screen.
The scene character glyph store for VIC bank $4000 and character-base bits 3–1 of $D018 set to 7. A character occupies eight consecutive bytes.
The top half of this scene set, from character code $80. The eight-byte glyph slots are used for the scene-specific objects and screen details.
